newsitem.title: SPAIN: ENDESA PULLS BACK AFTER HEFTY GAINS.
newsitem.headline: ENDESA PULLS BACK AFTER HEFTY GAINS.

text.p: Shares in Spanish electricity group Endesa took a tumble on Wednesday in what traders saw as a correction to recent sharp rises after a raft of good news.
Dealers said shares had been buoyed by talk that one or several local savings banks may be buying up shares ahead of the utility's public offering, set to begin in September.
By 0900 GMT, Endesa was trading 1.22 percent down at 3,235 pesetas, off an all time peak of 3,360 at the end of last month.
The Ibex-35 index of leading shares was 1.03 percent down at 6,747.62 after Spain's July CPI data disappointed the market and after a 1.26 percent slide on Wall Street overnight.
"Endesa has benefited from a big hand buying in recent sessions on the belief that a savings bank may take a stake in the electricity group ahead of privatisation," said one dealer.
Other dealers pointed out that there had been considerable block trading activity outside the market supporting the view that savings banks may be consolidating their holdings.
The government is set to sell a 35 percent stake in Endesa in the autumn.
Dealers said the stock had been supported by a good news in recent months including solid first half results and the purchase of a stake in Chile's Enersis.

Endesa announced last month it would purchase a controlling stake in power investment firm Enersis for a total $1.5 billion. Endesa said the acquisition would boost its sales and profits considerably.
